question: LCM and HCF of two numbers are 140 and 5 respectively. If one of the numbers is 35, then find the other number.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the direct relation: Other Number = (LCM × HCF) ÷ First Number

⇒ Other Number = (140 × 5) ÷ 35

⇒ Other Number = 4 × 5 = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

LCM of the two numbers = 140

HCF of the two numbers = 5

First number = 35

**Formula Used:**

First Number × Second Number = LCM × HCF

 
 1st Num × 2nd Num

 =

 
 LCM × HCF

 
 35 × ?

 =

 
 140 × 5

**Calculations:**

⇒ 35 × Second Number = 140 × 5

⇒ 35 × Second Number = 700

⇒ Second Number = 700 ÷ 35

⇒ Second Number = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and HCF of Fractions

LCM of fractions = LCM of numerators ÷ HCF of denominators. HCF of fractions = HCF of numerators ÷ LCM of denominators.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime if their HCF is 1. The LCM of two co-prime numbers is always equal to their product.

HCF as a Factor

The HCF of given numbers is always a perfect divisor (factor) of their LCM.
